sentences: Distributed subgraph detection asks whether a network contains a fixed constant-size graph H as a subgraph.
The source asks whether every such target can be detected in \(O(n) \mathrm{CONGEST}\) rounds or whether some targets require superlinear time.
A linear bound is easy for cliques, despite their prominence as hard patterns in centralized computation.
Other patterns can distribute their relevant edges across distant parts of the communication network in different ways, so centralized hardness is a poor guide.
A general upper bound or a superlinear example would establish a basic classification boundary for exact distributed pattern detection.
